chunks: And al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
The testimony of a slave from the people of the qiblah is valid against the People of the Book.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْقِبْلَةِ: those who face the qiblah, meaning Muslims
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: the People of the Book, such as Jews and Christians
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: legal testimony or witness statement in a judicial context

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a Muslim slave accepted against the People of the Book in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the admissibility of testimony in judicial matters. It states that the testimony of a mamluk who is from Ahl al-Qiblah is accepted against Ahl al-Kitab, indicating a distinction in evidentiary standing within this legal context.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3296 - And it was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:
"The testimony of a slave from the people of the Qiblah (Muslims) is valid against the People of the Book (Jews and Christians)."
